text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a flakey init race across Python/TS/Go SDKs when the Console pushes a routing-policy delta. Seen in canary and a customer prod replay.
kevin: repro steps? have logs?
maria: quick repro: start client, immediately call .predict while console API sends route update. sometimes client sets local fallback policy then overwrites with empty policy -> requests 403/invalid-route.
josiah: hmm, could be order of the async config handler vs default policy init. which SDK versions?
tina: @maria which versions? we recently shipped policy hot-reload in 1.12.0 (py) and 0.9.3 (ts).
maria: py 1.12.0, ts 0.9.3, go 0.8.1. attaching a short trace snippet: ```py
E 2026-03-21T15:04:12Z client.go:242 invalid route: ""
# caused by policyHandler.apply({}) setting route=null after client default applied
```
kevin: can we add a barrier so client default policy applies last? or make policy handler idempotent to empty payload?
josiah: prefer making handler resilient: ignore empty or ephemeral deltas if client hasn't finished init. but detecting init complete is tricky across languages.
tina: SDKs have init hooks. py/ts expose on_ready. maybe policy handler should queue deltas until on_ready or a 200ms settle window.
maria: queueing works but we need safety for long cold starts. queue with TTL 5s then apply latest. if not ready after TTL, apply latest non-empty or keep default.
kevin: can we add server-side change to avoid emitting blank policy on incremental updates? Console team, thoughts? @eng-platform
eng-bot: FYI: console push that emits policy deltas currently sends a remove-key update when no change; that's intentional for housekeeping.
josiah: ugh. then client defensiveness is best. implement queue+ttl in all SDKs. small patch in py/ts/go.
tina: I'll open a short RFC with patches and compat notes for changelog (mentioning behavior for on_ready).
maria: also add an e2e smoke in our canary flow to hit policy hot-reload.
kevin: workaround for customers: set explicit routing header in requests for now. docs PR?
maria: yep I'll post a short note in #support and add a snippet.
josiah: will draft patches. who wants to review py & ts?
tina: I can review py. kevin will take ts. josiah you take go?
josiah: yep.
kevin: estimate 2-3 days to land + canary.
maria: thanks. filing followups: GH issues for each SDK + canary job update. :thumbsup:
